label: the present perfect: I have done it
note: CLOSED BY CHAPTER 111, AND THE OLD NOTE WAS HALF STALE. 'Neither the participle nor the construction appears' -- the participle half is FALSE (ML-C90-past-participle teaches vanna at sequence 3180, and establishes its regularity, which is what A1-V-10 and A1-V-14 ask about); the construction half is TRUE (a census for -ittu returned zero files). The chapter costs NO vocabulary: the past vannu (ML-C32-varuka) and undu (ML-C32-undu, whose gloss already read '[someone] has') were both long owned, and only the join was missing. It is taught as four shapes off one past form -- vannu, vanna, vannittu, vannittundu -- each the one above it with a single change, contrasting a vowel sign taken OFF against -ittu put ON.
